name: voice
description: Talking to Jackson the way a user does, with the VM's own speech for a microphone: `sos install voice`, a virtual microphone (pw-loopback; the voice service listens to it through SVOYA_VOICE_SOURCE), phrases spoken by espeak-ng into it, the microphone opened from the panel's IPC (`jackson talk`). «который час» is answered by the fast path, then Jackson listens again by himself (conversation) and «спасибо, всё» ends it. A helper follows the voice service's journal and speaks each phrase when it says it listens. The VM has a sound card whose output is recorded: speaker.ogg is what Jackson said.

steps.text: sos install voice --yes && logger -t sos-vm-test SOS-STEP voice-ready || logger -t sos-vm-test SOS-STEP voice-failed

clear; sudo apt-get install -y -qq espeak-ng >/dev/null; python3 -c "open('/tmp/q1.txt','w').write('\u043a\u043e\u0442\u043e\u0440\u044b\u0439 \u0447\u0430\u0441'); open('/tmp/q2.txt','w').write('\u0441\u043f\u0430\u0441\u0438\u0431\u043e, \u0432\u0441\u0451')"; espeak-ng -v ru -s 140 -f /tmp/q1.txt -w /tmp/q1.wav; espeak-ng -v ru -s 140 -f /tmp/q2.txt -w /tmp/q2.wav; logger -t sos-vm-test SOS-STEP phrases-ready

clear; mkdir -p ~/.config/svoya; echo SVOYA_VOICE_SOURCE=vmic >~/.config/svoya/voice.env; (pw-loopback -m '[ MONO ]' --capture-props='media.class=Audio/Sink node.name=vmic-in' --playback-props='media.class=Audio/Source node.name=vmic node.description=vmic' >/dev/null 2>&1 &); sleep 2; systemctl --user start svoya-voice; wpctl status | grep -A4 -i sources

steps.pattern: voice ready in|voice models did not load

steps.text: clear; (journalctl --user -f -n0 -u svoya-voice | while read -r l; do case "$l" in *'listening (tap)'*) sleep 1; pw-play --target vmic-in /tmp/q1.wav;; *'listening (follow)'*) sleep 1; pw-play --target vmic-in /tmp/q2.wav;; esac; done >/dev/null 2>&1 &); sleep 1; quickshell -p /usr/share/svoya/shell ipc call jackson talk
